108. Kathaṃ sametassāti kathaṃ paṭipannassa. Vibhoti rūpanti rūpaṃ vibhavati, na bhaveyya vā. Sukhaṃ dukhañcāti iṭṭhāniṭṭharūpameva pucchati.

108. ‘How for one who is harmonized?’ means how for one who has practiced. ‘Form vanishes’ means form vanishes, or would not come to be. ‘Pleasure and pain’ means he asks only about desirable and undesirable form.

Jāneyyāmāti [V 0.0287] jānissāma. Ājāneyyāmāti visesena jānissāma. Vijāneyyāmāti anekavidhena jānissāma. Paṭivijāneyyāmāti sammā jānissāma. Paṭivijjheyyāmāti cittena bujjhissāma.

‘We would know’ means we will know. ‘We would know thoroughly’ means we will know distinctly. ‘We would discern’ means we will know in many ways. ‘We would know in detail’ means we will know rightly. ‘We would penetrate’ means we will understand with the mind.

109. Na saññasaññīti yathā sametassa vibhoti rūpaṃ, so pakatisaññāya saññīpi na hoti. Na visaññasaññīti visaññāyapi virūpāya saññāya visaññī na hoti ummattako vā khittacitto vā. Nopi asaññīti saññāvirahitopi na hoti nirodhasamāpanno vā asaññasatto vā. Na vibhūtasaññīti “sabbaso rūpasaññāna”ntiādinā (vibha. 508) nayena samatikkantasaññīpi na hoti arūpajjhānalābhī. Evaṃ sametassa vibhoti rūpanti etasmiṃ saññasaññitādibhāve aṭṭhatvā yadetaṃ vuttaṃ “so evaṃ [P 2.0357] samāhite citte…pe… ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattipaṭilābhatthāya cittaṃ abhinīharatī”ti, evaṃ sametassa arūpamaggasamaṅgino vibhoti rūpaṃ. Saññānidānā hi papañcasaṅkhāti evaṃ paṭipannassāpi ca yā saññā, taṃnidānā taṇhādiṭṭhipapañcāssa appahīnāva hontīti dasseti.

109. ‘Not a perceiver of perception’ means that just as for one who is harmonized, form vanishes, so he is not a perceiver with normal perception. ‘Not a perceiver of distorted perception’ means he does not perceive with distorted or perverted perception, nor is he insane or deranged in mind. ‘Nor without perception’ means he is not devoid of perception, like one attained to cessation or an insensible being. ‘Nor with perception vanished’ means he has not gone beyond perception by the method beginning with “by completely transcending perceptions of form” (Vibh 508), nor is he one who has attained the formless jhānas. ‘Thus, for one who is harmonized, form vanishes’: not remaining in this state of being a perceiver of perception and so forth, that which is said: ‘With his mind thus concentrated… he directs his mind toward the attainment of the attainment of the base of infinite space’—thus, for one who is harmonized, endowed with the formless path, form vanishes. ‘For perception is the origin of proliferation’: it is shown that even for one practicing thus, the craving, views, and proliferation rooted in perception are not yet abandoned.

Asaññino vuccanti nirodhasamāpannāti saññāvedanā nirodhetvā nirodhasamāpannā saññābhāvena asaññinoti kathīyanti. Asaññasattāti sabbena sabbaṃ saññābhāvena asaññabhave nibbattā.

‘Those who are without perception are called “attained to cessation”’ means that having ceased perception and feeling, those attained to cessation are said to be without perception because of the absence of perception. ‘The beings without perception’ are those entirely reborn in the realm of non-perception due to the complete absence of perception.

So evaṃ samāhite citteti tattha soti so bhikkhu. Evanti catutthajjhānakkamanidassanametaṃ, iminā kamena catutthajjhānaṃ paṭilabhitvāti vuttaṃ [M 0.0314] hoti. Samāhiteti iminā catutthajjhānasamādhinā samāhite. Parisuddhetiādīsu pana upekkhāsatipārisuddhibhāvena parisuddhe. Parisuddhattāyeva pariyodāte, pabhassareti vuttaṃ hoti. Sukhādīnaṃ paccayānaṃ ghātena vihatarāgādiaṅgaṇattā anaṅgaṇe. Anaṅgaṇattā eva ca vigatūpakkilese. Aṅgaṇena hi cittaṃ upakkilissati. Subhāvitattā mudubhūte, vasībhāvappatteti vuttaṃ hoti. Vase vattamānañhi cittaṃ mudūti vuccati. Muduttāyeva ca kammaniye, kammakkhame kammayoggeti vuttaṃ hoti. Mudu hi cittaṃ kammaniyaṃ hoti suddhantamiva suvaṇṇaṃ. Tadubhayampi ca subhāvitattāyeva. Yathāha “nāhaṃ, bhikkhave, aññaṃ ekadhammampi samanupassāmi, yaṃ evaṃ bhāvitaṃ kammaniyaṃ hoti yathayidaṃ, bhikkhave, citta”nti (a. ni. 1.22).

‘With the mind thus concentrated’: here ‘so’ refers to that bhikkhu. ‘Thus’ indicates this is a demonstration of the method for the fourth jhāna; by this method, it is said, the fourth jhāna is attained. ‘Concentrated’ means concentrated with the concentration of the fourth jhāna. In ‘purified’ and so on, it is purified by the purity of equanimity and mindfulness. Because it is purified, it is brightened and radiant. Due to the destruction of the conditions for pleasure and so on, it is free from the stains of passion and other defilements, thus ‘unstained.’ And because it is unstained, it is free from corruptions. For the mind is corrupted by stains. Because it is well-developed, it is pliable, and it is said to have attained mastery. For the mind that operates under mastery is called pliable. And because of its pliability, it is workable, capable of work, and fit for work. A pliable mind is workable, like refined gold. Both of these qualities are due to being well-developed. As it is said: ‘Monks, I do not see even one other thing that, when developed, becomes as workable as this, the mind’ (AN 1.22).

Etesu hi parisuddhabhāvādīsu ṭhitattā ṭhite. Ṭhitattāyeva āneñjappatte acale niriñjaneti vuttaṃ [V 0.0288] hoti. Mudukammaññabhāvena vā attano vase ṭhitattā ṭhite. Saddhādīhi pariggahitattā āneñjappatte. Saddhāpariggahitañhi cittaṃ assaddhiyena na iñjati, vīriyapariggahitaṃ kosajjena na iñjati, satipariggahitaṃ pamādena na iñjati, samādhipariggahitaṃ uddhaccena na iñjati, paññāpariggahitaṃ avijjāya na iñjati, obhāsagataṃ kilesandhakārena na iñjati. Imehi chahi dhammehi pariggahituṃ āneñjappattaṃ hoti. Evaṃ [P 2.0358] aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgataṃ cittaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ hoti ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattipaṭilābhatthāya.

Because it is established in these states of purity and so on, it is ‘established.’ Being established, it is said to be ‘unshaken,’ ‘immovable,’ and ‘unagitated.’ Or, due to its pliable and workable nature, because it remains under one’s control, it is ‘established.’ Being encompassed by faith and other qualities, it becomes ‘unshaken.’ For a mind encompassed by faith is not shaken by faithlessness, a mind encompassed by energy is not shaken by sloth, a mind encompassed by mindfulness is not shaken by heedlessness, a mind encompassed by concentration is not shaken by restlessness, a mind encompassed by wisdom is not shaken by ignorance, a mind that has attained illumination is not shaken by the darkness of defilements. Being encompassed by these six qualities, it becomes unshaken. Thus, a mind endowed with these eight factors becomes fit for application for the attainment of the attainment of the base of infinite space.

Aparo nayo – catutthajjhānasamādhinā samāhite. Nīvaraṇadūrībhāvena parisuddhe. Vitakkādisamatikkamena pariyodāte. Jhānapaṭilābhapaccanikānaṃ pāpakānaṃ icchāvacarānañca abhāvena anaṅgaṇe. Icchāvacarānanti icchāya avacarānaṃ, icchāvasena otiṇṇānaṃ pavattānaṃ nānappakārānaṃ kopaappaccayānanti attho. Abhijjhādīnaṃ cittūpakkilesānaṃ vigamena vigatūpakkilese. Ubhayampi cetaṃ aṅgaṇasuttavatthasuttānusāreneva (ma. ni. 1.57 ādayo, 70 ādayo) veditabbaṃ. Vasippattiyā mudubhūte. Iddhipādabhāvūpagamanena kammaniye. Bhāvanāpāripūriyā paṇītabhāvūpagamena ṭhite āneñjappatte, yathā āneñjabhāvaṃ āneñjappattaṃ hoti, evaṃ ṭhiteti attho. Evampi aṭṭhaṅgasamannāgamena cittaṃ abhinīhārakkhamaṃ hoti ākāsānañcāyatanasamāpattipaṭilābhatthāya pādakaṃ padaṭṭhānabhūtaṃ.

Another method: ‘concentrated’ through the concentration of the fourth jhāna. ‘Purified’ by the removal of the hindrances. ‘Brightened’ by transcending thought and the like. ‘Unblemished’ by the absence of evil qualities that oppose the attainment of jhāna, and by the absence of things that move in the sphere of desire. ‘Things that move in the sphere of desire’ means things that move by desire, that is, the various kinds of anger and displeasure that arise having fallen under the sway of desire. ‘Free from defilements’ by the removal of mental corruptions such as covetousness. Both of these should be understood in accordance with the Aṅgaṇasutta and the Vatthasutta (MN 5, MN 7). ‘Pliable’ by the attainment of mastery. ‘Workable’ by having approached the state of the bases of psychic power. ‘Established’ and ‘unshaken’ by reaching a sublime state through the perfection of development—the meaning is that just as it has attained the unshaken state, so it is established. In this way too, endowed with eight factors, the mind becomes capable of being directed—serving as a foundation and a proximate cause for the attainment of the attainment of the base of infinite space.

Āruppamaggasamaṅgīti [M 0.0315] arūpasamāpattiyā gamanamaggena aparihīno. Papañcāyeva papañcasaṅkhāti taṇhādipapañcāyeva papañcasaṅkhā.

‘Endowed with the formless path’ means one who has not fallen away from the path leading to the formless attainments. ‘Proliferation of concepts’ is just proliferation itself, that is, the proliferation of concepts consisting of craving and so forth.

110. Ettāvataggaṃ nu vadanti heke, yakkhassa suddhiṃ idha paṇḍitāse. Udāhu aññampi vadanti ettoti ettāvatā nu idha paṇḍitā samaṇabrāhmaṇā aggaṃ suddhiṃ sattassa vadanti, udāhu aññampi etto arūpasamāpattito adhikañca vadantīti pucchati.

110. ‘Do some wise ones here declare just this much to be the highest purity for a being? Or do they speak of something else beyond this?’ – thus he asks: ‘Do some wise ascetics and brahmins here declare only this much to be the highest purity of a being, or do they speak of something more, something beyond this formless attainment?’

Etto arūpasamāpattitoti etasmā arūpasamāpattito.

‘Beyond this formless attainment’ means from this formless attainment.

111. Ettāvataggampi vadanti heketi eke sassatavādā samaṇabrāhmaṇā paṇḍitamānino ettāvatāpi aggaṃ suddhiṃ vadanti. Tesaṃ paneke samayaṃ vadantīti tesaññeva eke ucchedavādā samayaṃ ucchedaṃ vadanti. Anupādisese kusalāvadānāti anupādisese kusalavādā samānā.

111. ‘Some declare even this much to be the highest’ – some eternalist ascetics and brahmins, conceited as wise, declare even this to be the highest purity. ‘But some of them declare a time’ – some others among them, the annihilationists, declare annihilation. ‘Skilled in what is without remainder’ means being skilled proponents regarding the state without remainder.

Bhavatajjitāti [V 0.0289] bhavato bhītā. Vibhavaṃ abhinandantīti ucchedaṃ [P 2.0359] paṭicca tussanti. Te sattassa samanti te ucchedavādino puggalassa samaṃ anuppattiṃ vadanti. Upasamanti atīva samaṃ. Vūpasamanti santaṃ. Nirodhanti anuppādaṃ. Paṭipassaddhinti apunuppattiṃ.

‘Terrified by existence’ means fearful of existence. ‘They delight in non-existence’ means they are pleased in reliance on annihilation. ‘They speak of a being’s pacification’ means those annihilationists speak of a person’s pacification, that is, non-arising. ‘They are fully pacified’ means exceedingly pacified. ‘They are calmed’ means at peace. ‘They cease’ means non-arising. ‘They are tranquil’ means non-re-arising.

112. Ete ca ñatvā upanissitāti ete ca diṭṭhigatike sassatucchedadiṭṭhiyo nissitāti ñatvā. Ñatvā munī nissaye so vīmaṃsīti nissaye ca ñatvā so vīmaṃsī paṇḍito buddhamuni. Ñatvā vimuttoti dukkhāniccādito dhamme ñatvā vimutto. Bhavābhavāya na sametīti punappunaṃ upapattiyā na samāgacchati. Aparāmasanti aparāmasanto. Parāmāsaṃ nāpajjantoti attho.

112. ‘And knowing these are dependent’ means knowing that these adherents of views are dependent on the views of eternalism and annihilationism. ‘Knowing the dependencies, the sage investigated’ means and knowing the dependencies, that wise Buddha-sage investigates. ‘Knowing, he is liberated’ means knowing the phenomena, beginning with suffering and impermanence, he is liberated. ‘He does not incline to existence and non-existence’ means he does not come to repeated rebirth. ‘Not grasping’ means not grasping. The meaning is: he does not fall into grasping.

Saddhammappajjotikāya mahāniddesaṭṭhakathāya

From the Saddhammappajjotikā, the Commentary on the Mahāniddesa.

Kalahavivādasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Kalahavivāda Sutta Niddesa is concluded.

12. Cūḷabyūhasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā

12. The Explanation of the Cūḷabyūha Sutta Niddesa

Dvādasame [V 0.0290][P 2.0360][M 0.0316] cūḷabyūhasuttaniddese sakaṃsakaṃdiṭṭhiparibbasānāti idampi tasmiṃyeva mahāsamaye “sabbepime diṭṭhigatikā ‘sādhurūpāmhā’ti bhaṇanti, kiṃ nu kho sādhurūpāva ime attano eva diṭṭhiyā patiṭṭhahanti, udāhu aññampi diṭṭhiṃ gaṇhantī”ti uppannacittānaṃ ekaccānaṃ devatānaṃ tamatthaṃ pakāsetuṃ purimanayeneva nimmitabuddhena attānaṃ pucchāpetvā vuttaṃ.

In the twelfth, the Cūḷabyūha Sutta Niddesa, regarding ‘dwelling in their respective views,’ this too was spoken during that great assembly. ‘All these adherents of views declare, “We are of a good nature.” But are these of a good nature established only in their own view, or do they adopt other views as well?’ This was said to clarify the matter for certain deities in whom such a thought had arisen. Following the previous method, it was spoken after a created Buddha was made to ask the question of himself.

113. Tattha ādito dvepi gāthā pucchāgāthāyeva. Tāsu sakaṃ sakaṃ diṭṭhiparibbasānāti attano attano diṭṭhiyā vasamānā. Viggayha nānā kusalā vadantīti taṃ diṭṭhiṃ balavaggāhaṃ gahetvā “tattha kusalāmhā”ti paṭijānamānā puthu puthu vadanti, ekaṃ na vadanti. Yo evaṃ jānāti sa vedi dhammaṃ, idaṃ paṭikkosamakevalī soti tañca diṭṭhiṃ sandhāya yo evaṃ jānāti, so dhammaṃ vediyi. Idaṃ pana paṭikkosanto hīno hotīti ca vadanti.

113. Herein, the first two verses are indeed question verses. In them, ‘sakaṃ sakaṃ diṭṭhiparibbasānā’ means abiding under the sway of their own respective views. ‘Viggayha nānā kusalā vadanti’ means, having firmly grasped that view with forceful insistence, they declare, ‘We are skilled in that,’ and they speak separately, not as one. ‘Yo evaṃ jānāti sa vedi dhammaṃ, idaṃ paṭikkosamakevalī so’ means, with reference to that view, that one who knows thus understands the Dhamma, and they also say that one who rejects this is inferior.

Nānā vadantīti nānākāraṇaṃ bhaṇanti. Vividhaṃ vadantīti nānāvidhaṃ bhaṇanti. Aññoññaṃ vadantīti ekaṃ avatvā aññaṃ aññaṃ gahetvā vadanti. Akevalī soti yo akusalo ayaṃ. Asamattoti na paripūro. Aparipuṇṇoti na sampuṇṇo.

‘Nānā vadanti’ means they speak for various reasons. ‘Vividhaṃ vadanti’ means they speak in different ways. ‘Aññoññaṃ vadanti’ means, not saying one thing, they take up one thing after another and speak. ‘Akevalī so’ means one who is unskillful. ‘Asamatto’ means not fully accomplished. ‘Aparipuṇṇo’ means not completely fulfilled.

114. Bāloti hīno. Akkusaloti avidvā.

114. ‘Bālo’ means inferior. ‘Akkusalo’ means unwise.

115. Idāni tisso vissajjanagāthā hontīti. Tā purimaḍḍhena vuttamatthaṃ pacchimaḍḍhena paṭibyūhitvā ṭhitā. Tena byūhena uttarasuttato ca appakattā idaṃ suttaṃ “cūḷabyūha”nti nāmaṃ labhi. Tattha paṭhamagāthāyaṃ tāva parassa ce dhammanti parassa diṭṭhiṃ. Sabbevime bālāti evaṃ sante sabbeva ime [P 2.0361] bālā hontīti adhippāyo. Kiṃkāraṇā? Sabbevime diṭṭhiparibbasānāti.

115. Now there are three verses of reply. These stand by refuting, with their latter half, the meaning stated in the first half. Due to this exposition and because it is shorter than the subsequent sutta, this sutta obtained the name ‘Cūḷabyūha’. Therein, in the first verse, ‘parassa ce dhammaṃ’ refers to the view of another. ‘Sabbevime bālā’ means that if this is so, then all these are fools. What is the reason? Because all are addicted to views.

116. Sandiṭṭhiyā [V 0.0291] ceva na vīvadātā, saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutīmāti sakāya diṭṭhiyā anavīvadātā avodātā saṃkiliṭṭhāva samānā saṃsuddhapaññā ca kusalā ca mutimanto ca te honti ce. Atha vā “sandiṭṭhiyā ce vadātā”ti pāṭho, tassattho – sakāya pana diṭṭhiyā vodātā [M 0.0317] saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutimanto honti ce, na tesaṃ kocīti evaṃ sante tesaṃ ekopi nihīnapañño na hoti, kiṃkāraṇā? Diṭṭhī hi tesampi tathā samattā, yathā itaresanti.

116. ‘Sandiṭṭhiyā ceva na vīvadātā, saṃsuddhapaññā kusalā mutīmā’ means that being unpurified by their own view, unpurified, and defiled, they are pure in wisdom, skilled, and possessed of understanding. Alternatively, the reading is ‘sandiṭṭhiyā ce vadātā’, the meaning of which is: if they are purified by their own view, pure in wisdom, skilled, and possessed of understanding, then none of them is of inferior wisdom. Why is that? Because their views are equally complete, just like those of others.

117. Na vāhametanti gāthāya saṅkhepattho – yaṃ te mithu dve dve janā aññamaññaṃ “bālo”ti āhu, ahaṃ etaṃ tathiyanti tacchanti neva brūmi. Kiṃkāraṇā? Yasmā sabbeva te sakaṃ sakaṃ diṭṭhiṃ “idameva saccaṃ moghamañña”nti akaṃsu, tena ca kāraṇena paraṃ “bālo”ti dahanti. Ettha ca tathiyaṃ, tathevanti (su. ni. aṭṭha. 2.889) dvepi pāṭhā.

117. The summary meaning of the verse ‘Na vāhametaṃ’ is this: When two people mutually call each other ‘fool,’ I do not declare that this is true. Why is that? Because all of them have each considered their own view as ‘this alone is the truth, others’ is vain,’ and for that reason they label others as ‘fools.’ Here, both readings ‘tathiyaṃ’ and ‘tatheva’ are acceptable.

Tacchanti atucchaṃ. Tathanti aviparītaṃ, bhūtanti santaṃ. Yāthāvanti saṃvijjamānaṃ. Aviparitanti na visaṅketaṃ.

‘Tacchaṃ’ means not empty. ‘Tathaṃ’ means not inverted. ‘Bhūtaṃ’ means existent. ‘Yāthāvaṃ’ means as it really is. ‘Aviparītaṃ’ means not distorted.

118. Yamāhūti pucchāgāthāya “yaṃ diṭṭhisaccaṃ tathiya”nti eke āhu.

118. ‘Yamāhu’ in the question verse means: some say, ‘A truth based on a view is real.’

119. Ekañhi saccanti vissajjanagāthāya ekaṃ saccaṃ nirodho maggo vā. Yasmiṃ pajā no vivade pajānanti yamhi sacce pajānanto pajā no vivadeyyuṃ. Sayaṃ thunantīti attanā vadanti.

119. In the verse of reply, ‘ekaṃ hi saccaṃ’ means the one truth: cessation or the path. ‘Yasmiṃ pajā no vivade pajānanti’ means: knowing which truth, beings would not dispute. ‘Sayaṃ thunanti’ means they speak for themselves.

120. Kasmā nūti pucchāgāthāya pavādiyāseti vādino. Udāhu te takkamanussarantīti te vādino udāhu attano takkamattaṃ anugacchanti.

120. In the question verse: ‘Kasmā nu’ means ‘Why then?’ ‘Pavādiyāse’ means debaters. ‘Udāhu te takkamanussaranti’ means: or do those debaters merely follow their own reasoning?

Takkapariyāhatanti vitakkena samantato āhataṃ. Vīmaṃsānucaritanti attano upaṭṭhitapaññāya vicaritaṃ. Sayaṃpaṭibhānanti attano paṭibhānaṃ.

‘Takkapariyāhataṃ’ means struck all around by thought. ‘Vīmaṃsānucaritaṃ’ means investigated by one’s own present wisdom. ‘Sayaṃpaṭibhānaṃ’ means one’s own intuition.

121. Na [P 2.0362] hevāti vissajjanagāthāya aññatra saññāya niccānīti ṭhapetvā saññāmattena niccanti gahitaggahaṇāni. Takkañca diṭṭhīsu pakappayitvāti attano niccasaṅkappamattaṃ diṭṭhīsu janetvā.

121. In the verse of reply beginning ‘Na heva...’, the phrase ‘aññatra saññāya niccāni’ means: except for those things grasped as permanent through mere perception. ‘Takkañca diṭṭhīsu pakappayitvā’ means: having generated in their views merely their own notion of permanence.

Yasmā [V 0.0292] pana diṭṭhīsu vitakkaṃ janentā diṭṭhiyo sañjanenti, tasmā vuttaṃ “diṭṭhigatāni janenti sañjanentī”tiādi. Janentīti uparūpari diṭṭhiṃ uppādentā janenti. Sañjanentītiādīni upasaggavasena padaṃ vaḍḍhetvā vuttāni. Mayhaṃ saccanti mama vacanaṃ tacchaṃ.

Since those who generate thoughts about views produce views, it is said, ‘They generate and produce views,’ and so on. ‘Janenti’ means they generate views again and again. ‘Sañjanenti’ and the like are stated by expanding the word with prefixes. ‘Mayhaṃ saccaṃ’ means ‘My word is true.’

122. Idāni [M 0.0318] evaṃ nānāsaccesu asantesu takkamattaṃ anussarantānaṃ diṭṭhigatikānaṃ vippaṭipattiṃ dassetuṃ “diṭṭhe sute”tiādikā gāthāyo abhāsi. Tattha diṭṭheti diṭṭhaṃ, diṭṭhasuddhinti adhippāyo. Esa nayo sutādīsu. Ete ca nissāya vimānadassīti ete diṭṭhidhamme nissayitvā suddhibhāvasaṅkhātaṃ vimānaṃ asammānaṃ passantopi. Vinicchaye ṭhatvā pahassamāno, bālo paro akkusaloti cāhāti evaṃ vimānadassīpi tasmiṃ diṭṭhivinicchaye ṭhatvā tuṭṭhijāto hāsajāto hutvā paro “hīno ca avidvā cā”ti evaṃ vadatiyeva.

122. Now, to show the wrong practice of those attached to views, who merely follow their own reasoning regarding various non-existent truths, the verses beginning with ‘diṭṭhe sute’ were spoken. Therein, ‘diṭṭhe’ refers to what is seen, with the meaning of ‘purity in what is seen.’ This same method applies to ‘suta’ and so forth. ‘Ete ca nissāya vimānadassī’ means: relying on these phenomena of view, one sees a ‘mansion’ (vimāna)—that is, a state considered to be purity—while also being disrespectful (asammānaṃ). ‘Vinicchaye ṭhatvā pahassamāno, bālo paro akkusaloti cāha’ means: thus, even one who sees this mansion, standing firm in that judgment based on view, becomes delighted and joyful, and says of another, ‘That person is inferior and unwise.’

Na sammānetītipi vimānadassīti na bahumānaṃ karotīti evampi vimānadassī na bahumānadassī. Domanassaṃ janetīti paṭhamaṃ diṭṭhinissayaṃ allīyitvā domanassaṃ patvā pacchā diṭṭhivinicchaye ṭhitakāle somanassaṃ uppādetīti attho.

‘Na sammānetītipi vimānadassī’ means: he does not show much respect; thus, one who is a ‘seer of a mansion’ (vimānadassī) is one who does not show much respect. ‘Domanassaṃ janeti’ means that first, by clinging to a reliance on view, one experiences displeasure, but later, when standing firm in a judgment based on view, one generates gladness—this is the meaning.

Vinicchayadiṭṭhiyā ṭhatvāti sanniṭṭhānaṃ katvā gahitadiṭṭhiyā ṭhatvā.

‘Vinicchayadiṭṭhiyā ṭhatvā’ means: having made a determination, standing firm in an adopted view.

123. Evaṃ sante yenevāti gāthā. Tattha sayamattanāti sayameva attānaṃ. Vimānetīti garahati. Tadeva pāvāti tadeva vacanaṃ diṭṭhiṃ vadati, taṃ vā puggalaṃ.

123. This being so, there is the verse beginning ‘Yeneva...’ Therein, ‘sayamattanā’ means by his own self. ‘Vimāneti’ means he censures. ‘Tadeva pāva’ means that very statement, view, or person.

124. Atisāradiṭṭhiyāti gāthāyattho – so evaṃ tāya lakkhaṇātisāriniyā atisāradiṭṭhiyā samatto paripuṇṇo uddhumāto, tena ca diṭṭhimānena matto “paripuṇṇo [P 2.0363] ahaṃ kevalī”ti evaṃ paripuṇṇamānī. Sayameva attānaṃ manasā “ahaṃ paṇḍito”ti abhisiñcati. Kiṃkāraṇā? Diṭṭhī hi sā tassa tathā samattāti.

124. The meaning of the verse on ‘atisāradiṭṭhiyā’ is this: He is thus complete, fulfilled, and inflated by that overbearing view which is characterized by excess. Intoxicated by that conceit based on his view, he is proud of his completeness, thinking, “I am complete, I am perfect.” He himself mentally anoints himself, thinking, “I am wise.” What is the reason? Because that view of his is so complete for him.

Sabbā tā diṭṭhiyo lakkhaṇātikkantāti tā sabbā dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhiyo lakkhaṇaṃ atītā atisarantīti atikkantā. Anomoti anūno.

‘Sabbā tā diṭṭhiyo lakkhaṇātikkantā’ means that all those sixty-two views have gone beyond their characteristic, surpassing it. ‘Anomo’ means not deficient.

125. Parassa ceti gāthāya sambandho attho ca – kiñca bhiyyo? Yo so vinicchaye ṭhatvā pahassamāno “bālo paro akkusalo”ti cāha, tassa parassa ce hi vacasā so tena vuccamāno [V 0.0293] nihīno hoti, tumo sahā hoti nihīnapañño, sopi teneva saha nihīnapañño hoti. Sopi hi taṃ “bālo”ti vadati. Atha tassa [M 0.0319] vacanaṃ appamāṇaṃ, so pana sayameva vedagū ca dhīro ca hoti. Evaṃ sante na koci bālo samaṇesu atthi. Sabbepi hi te attano icchāya paṇḍitā.

125. The connection and meaning of the verse beginning ‘Parassa ce...’ is this—and what more? If the one who stands firm in his judgment, laughing and saying, “The other is a fool, unskillful,” makes that other person inferior by his words when he says this, then he himself (tumo) is also of inferior wisdom along with him. For he too calls the other a “fool.” If, on the other hand, the other’s word is not authoritative, while he himself is a knower of the truth and wise, then, this being so, there is no fool among the ascetics, for they are all wise by their own estimation.

Vācāyāti kathanena. Vacanenāti bhāsitena. Ninditakāraṇāti garahahetunā. Garahitakāraṇāti avaññātahetunā. Upavaditakāraṇāti upavādahetunā.

‘Vācāya’ means by speaking. ‘Vacanena’ means by what is spoken. ‘Ninditakāraṇā’ means for the reason of censure. ‘Garahitakāraṇā’ means for the reason of contempt. ‘Upavaditakāraṇā’ means for the reason of reproach.

126. Aññaṃ itoti gāthāya sambandho attho ca – “atha ce sayaṃ vedagū hoti dhīro. Na koci bālo samaṇesu atthī”ti evañhi vuttepi siyā kassaci “kasmā”ti. Tattha vuccate – yasmā aññaṃ ito yābhivadanti dhammaṃ, aparaddhā suddhimakevalī te. Evampi titthyā puthuso vadanti, ye ito aññaṃ diṭṭhiṃ abhivadanti, te aparaddhā viraddhā suddhimaggaṃ, akevalino ca teti evaṃ puthutitthiyā yasmā vadantīti vuttaṃ hoti. Kasmā panevaṃ vadantīti ce? Sandiṭṭhirāgena hi tebhirattā, yasmā sakena diṭṭhirāgena te abhirattāti vuttaṃ hoti.

126. The connection and meaning of the verse beginning 'another than this' is as follows. 'But if he himself is one who has attained knowledge and is wise, there is no fool among ascetics.' Even when this is said, someone might ask, 'Why?' To this it is said: 'Because those who proclaim a doctrine other than this have erred; they are not complete in purity.' Thus do the sectarians speak variously. Those who proclaim a view other than this have erred, have deviated from the path of purity, and are not complete. Thus it is said that the various sectarians speak. And why do they speak thus? 'Because they are impassioned by the lust for their own view'; that is to say, because they are infatuated with their own view.

Te suddhimagganti te aññatitthiyā akiliṭṭhamaggaṃ. Visuddhimagganti niddosamaggaṃ. Parisuddhimagganti sukkamaggaṃ. Vodātamagganti paṇḍaramaggaṃ. Pariyodātamagganti pabhāvantamaggaṃ. Viraddhāti vuttavidhinā maggena virajjhitvā ṭhitā. Aparaddhāti aparajjhitvā ṭhitā. Khalitāti [P 2.0364] parihīnā. Galitāti tato bhaṭṭhā. Aññāyāti aññāṇena. Aparaddhāti parājayamāpannā. Atha vā “ñāyāparaddhā”tipi pāṭho. Ñāyena maggena viraddhāti attho.

'They' refers to the other sectarians. 'Path of purity' means the undefiled path. 'Path of purification' means the faultless path. 'Thoroughly purified path' means the pure path. 'Immaculate path' means the bright white path. 'Perfectly pure path' means the shining path. 'Strayed' means having become separated from the path in the way described. 'Failed' means having erred. 'Faltered' means having declined. 'Collapsed' means having fallen from that. 'Through ignorance' means through lack of knowledge. 'Failed' means having met with defeat. Alternatively, there is also the reading 'failed in the right method.' The meaning is 'strayed from the path which is the right method.'

127. Evaṃ abhirattā ca – idheva suddhinti gāthā. Tattha sakāyaneti sakamagge. Daḷhaṃ vadānāti daḷhavādā.

127. And being thus infatuated, there is the verse: 'Here alone is purity.' Therein, 'in their own path' (sakāyane) means in their own path (sakamagge). 'Speaking firmly' (daḷhaṃ vadānā) means those who hold firm views (daḷhavādā).

Thiravādāti sanniṭṭhānavādā. Balikavādāti balavantavādā. Avaṭṭhitavādāti patiṭṭhahitvā kathitavādā.

'Those of steadfast tenets' (thiravādā) means those who hold resolute views. 'Those of forceful tenets' (balikavādā) means those who hold powerful views. 'Those of unwavering tenets' (avaṭṭhitavādā) means those who speak after having firmly established their views.

128. Ye evañca daḷhavādā, tesu yo koci titthiyo sakāyane vāpi daḷhaṃ vadāno kamettha bāloti paraṃ daheyya, saṅkhepato tattha sassatucchedasaṅkhāte vitthārato natthikaissarakārakaniyatiādibhede sake ayane “idameva sacca”nti daḷhaṃ vadāno kaṃ paraṃ ettha diṭṭhigate [V 0.0294] “bālo”ti saha dhammena passeyya, nanu sabbopi tassa matena paṇḍito [M 0.0320] eva suppaṭipanno eva ca. Evaṃ sante sayameva so medhagamāvaheyya, paraṃ vadaṃ bālamasuddhidhammaṃ. Sopi paraṃ “bālo ca asuddhidhammo ca aya”nti vadanto attanāva kalahaṃ āvaheyya. Kasmā? Yasmā sabbopi tassa matena paṇḍitoyeva suppaṭipannoyeva ca.

128. Among those who hold such firm views, what sectarian, firmly asserting his own doctrine, could consider another here a fool? Firmly asserting in his own doctrine—whether briefly, regarding what are classified as eternalism and annihilationism, or in detail, regarding the divisions of nihilism, divine creationism, determinism, and the like—that 'This alone is true,' whom else here, in the matter of views, could he rightly see as a 'fool'? Surely, according to his own opinion, everyone is wise and well-practiced. This being so, he would bring about a quarrel for himself by calling another a fool and of impure doctrine. He, by calling another 'a fool and of impure doctrine,' would bring conflict upon himself. Why? Because according to his own opinion, everyone is indeed wise and well-practiced.

129. Evaṃ sabbathāpi vinicchaye ṭhatvā sayaṃ pamāya, uddhaṃ sa lokasmiṃ vivādametīti diṭṭhiyā ṭhatvā sayañca satthārādiṃ minitvā so bhiyyo vivādametīti. Evaṃ pana vinicchayesu ādīnavaṃ ñatvā ariyamaggena hitvāna sabbāni vinicchayāni, na medhagaṃ kubbati jantu loketi arahattanikūṭena desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi.

129. The line 'Thus, having stood firm in judgment in every way and measured for oneself, one further comes to dispute in the world' means: standing firm in a view and having measured oneself, the Teacher, and so on, one engages in dispute all the more. However, having known the danger in such judgments and having abandoned all judgments by means of the Noble Path, he concluded the teaching with the pinnacle of Arahantship with the words: 'a being does not create conflict in the world.'

Sayaṃ pamāyāti attanā minitvā. Paminitvāti pamāṇaṃ katvā. “Pavinetvā”tipi pāṭho, taṃ na sundaraṃ. Uddhaṃ vādena saddhinti attano upari kathentena saha. Desanāpariyosāne purābhedasutte (mahāni. 83) vuttasadiso eva abhisamayo ahosīti.

'Having measured for oneself' (sayaṃ pamāya) means having measured by oneself. 'Having measured' (paminitvā) means having made a standard. 'Having removed' (pavinetvā) is also a reading, but it is not good. 'With arrogant speech' (uddhaṃ vādena saddhiṃ) means together with one who speaks of himself in a superior way. At the conclusion of the teaching, a realization occurred just like the one described in the Purābheda Sutta (Mahāniddesa 83).

Saddhammappajjotikāya mahāniddesaṭṭhakathāya

From the Saddhammappajjotikā, the commentary on the Mahāniddesa.

Cūḷabyūhasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

Here ends the explanation of the Cūḷabyūhasutta Niddesa.

13. Mahābyūhasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā

13. The Explanation of the Mahābyūhasutta Niddesa

130. Terasame [P 2.0365][V 0.0295] mahābyūhasuttaniddese ye kecime diṭṭhiparibbasānāti idampi “kiṃ nu kho ime diṭṭhiparibbasānā viññūnaṃ santikā nindameva labhanti, udāhu pasaṃsampī”ti uppannacittānaṃ ekaccānaṃ devatānaṃ tamatthaṃ āvikātuṃ purimanayeneva nimmitabuddhena attānaṃ pucchāpetvā vuttaṃ. Tattha anvānayantīti anu ānayanti punappunaṃ āharanti.

130. In the thirteenth Mahābyūhasutta Niddesa, the passage beginning 'Whoever these wanderers in views are' was also spoken by the created Buddha, who had caused himself to be questioned in the same way as before, in order to reveal the meaning to certain deities in whose minds this thought had arisen: 'What indeed do these wanderers in views receive from the wise? Do they receive only blame, or praise as well?' Therein, 'they incur' (anvānayanti) means they bring after, they bring again and again.

Nindameva anventīti garahameva upagacchanti.

'They incur only blame' (nindameva anventi) means they meet with only censure.

131. Idāni yasmā te “idameva sacca”nti vadantāpi diṭṭhigatikavādino kadāci katthaci pasaṃsampi labhanti, yaṃ etaṃ pasaṃsāsaṅkhātaṃ vādaphalaṃ, taṃ appaṃ, rāgādīnaṃ samāya samatthaṃ na hoti, ko pana vādo dutiye nindāphale, tasmā [M 0.0321] etamatthaṃ dassento imaṃ tāva vissajjanagāthaṃ āha “appañhi etaṃ na alaṃ samāya, duve vivādassa phalāni brūmī”ti. Tattha duve vivādassa phalānīti nindā ca pasaṃsā ca jayaparājayādīni vā taṃsabhāgāni. Etampi disvāti “nindā aniṭṭhā eva, pasaṃsā nālaṃ samāyā”ti etampi vivādaphale ādīnavaṃ disvā. Khemābhipassaṃ avivādabhūminti avivādabhūmiṃ nibbānaṃ khemanti passamāno.

131. Now, because those adherents of speculative views, even while saying, 'This alone is the truth,' do sometimes and somewhere receive praise, yet that fruit of debate known as praise is insignificant and is not capable of bringing about the calming of lust and so forth—what then to say of the second fruit, blame? Therefore, showing this meaning, he first spoke this explanatory verse: 'For this is little and not enough for calm; I declare the two fruits of dispute.' Therein, 'the two fruits of dispute' means blame and praise, or victory, defeat, and other similar things. 'Seeing this too' (etampi disvā) means seeing this danger in the fruits of dispute: 'Blame is indeed undesirable, and praise is not enough for calm.' 'Seeing the ground of non-dispute as safe' (khemābhipassaṃ avivādabhūmiṃ) means seeing the ground of non-dispute, Nibbāna, as safety.

Appakanti mandaṃ. Parittakanti thokaṃ. Omakanti heṭṭhimakaṃ. Lāmakanti pāpakaṃ. Samāyāti rāgādīnaṃ samanatthāya. Upasamāyāti uparūpari samanatthāya. Vūpasamāyāti sannisīdāpanatthāya. Nibbānāyāti amatamahānibbānatthāya. Paṭinissaggāyāti maggena kilesānaṃ nissajjanatthāya. Paṭipassaddhiyāti phalena paṭipassaddhānaṃ anuppajjanatthāya nālaṃ.

'Little' (appakaṃ) means insignificant. 'Limited' (parittakaṃ) means small. 'Low' (omakaṃ) means inferior. 'Bad' (lāmakaṃ) means poor. It is not adequate 'for calm' (samāya), that is, for the purpose of calming lust and so forth; 'for appeasement' (upasamāya), that is, for the purpose of calming again and again; 'for allaying' (vūpasamāya), that is, for the purpose of settling down; 'for Nibbāna' (nibbānāya), that is, for the purpose of the deathless, great Nibbāna; 'for relinquishment' (paṭinissaggāya), that is, for the purpose of relinquishing the defilements by means of the path; 'for tranquility' (paṭipassaddhiyā), that is, for the purpose of the non-arising of what has been tranquilized by means of the fruit.

132. Evañhi avivādamāno – yā kācimāti gāthā. Tattha sammutiyoti diṭṭhiyo. Puthujjāti puthujjanasambhavā. So [P 2.0366] upayaṃ kimeyyāti so upagantabbaṭṭhena upayaṃ rūpādīsu ekampi [V 0.0296] dhammaṃ kiṃ upeyya, kena vā kāraṇena upeyya. Diṭṭhe sute khantimakubbamānoti diṭṭhasutasuddhīsu pemaṃ akaronto.

132. Thus, not engaging in dispute—the verse 'Whatever these...' Therein, 'conventions' means views. 'Of the common folk' means arising from ordinary people. 'What means would he approach?' means: what one thing among forms and so forth, which is a means in the sense that it is to be approached, would he approach, or for what reason should he approach it? 'Not making acceptance in what is seen or heard' means not creating affection for purities based on what is seen and heard.

Puthujjanehi janitāti puthujjanehi uppāditā. Sammutiyoti diṭṭhiyo. Puthu nānājanehi janitā vāti anekavidhehi diṭṭhigatikehi uppāditā vā. Netīti na eti. Na upetīti samīpaṃ na eti. Na upagacchatīti nivattati. Nābhinivisatīti pavisitvā nappatiṭṭhati.

'Generated by common folk' means produced by ordinary people. 'Conventions' means views. 'Or generated by many different people' means or produced by many kinds of adherents of views. 'He does not go' means he does not go. 'He does not approach' means he does not come near. 'He does not go to' means he turns away. 'He does not adhere' means having entered, he does not become established.

133. Ito bāhirā pana – sīluttamāti gāthā tassattho – sīlaṃyeva “uttama”nti maññamānā sīluttamāti eke bhonto saṃyamamattena suddhiṃ vadanti, hatthivatādiñca vataṃ samādāya upaṭṭhitāse. Idheva diṭṭhiyaṃ assa satthuno suddhiṃ bhavūpanītā bhavajjhositā samānā vadanti, api ca te kusalāvadānā “kusalā maya”nti evaṃvādā.

133. But as for those outside of this, there is the verse beginning 'Virtue is supreme.' Its meaning is as follows: some venerable ones, considering virtue alone as 'supreme,' are called 'those for whom virtue is supreme.' They declare purity by mere restraint, and are devoted to it, having undertaken observances such as the elephant-observance. Being led on by becoming and attached to existence, they declare the purity of their own teacher in this very view. Furthermore, they who claim to be skilled speak thus: 'We are skilled.'

134. Evaṃ sīluttamesu ca tesu tathā paṭipanno yo koci – sace cutoti gāthā. Tassattho – sace tato sīlavatato paravicchindanena vā anabhisambhuṇanto vā cuto hoti, so taṃ sīlabbatakammaṃ puññābhisaṅkhārādikammaṃ vā virādhayitvā vedhatī. Na kevalañca vedhati[M 0.0322], api ca kho taṃ sīlabbatasuddhiṃ pajappatī ca vippalapati ca patthayatī ca. Kimiva? Satthāva hīno pavasaṃ gharamhā, gharamhā pavasanto satthato hīno yathā taṃ gharaṃ vā satthaṃ vā patthayatīti.

134. And thus, for whoever practices in such a way among those who hold virtue as supreme, there is the verse: 'If he should fall away.' Its meaning is as follows: if he falls away from that virtue and observance, either by being cut off by another or by not being able to accomplish it, he trembles, having failed in that action of virtue and observance, or that action of meritorious formation and so on. And not only does he tremble, but he also yearns for, laments, and longs for that purity of virtue and observance. Just as what? Just as one separated from a caravan while away from home, or one away from home and separated from a caravan, longs for that home or caravan.

Paravicchindanāya vāti parena vāriyamāno vā. Anabhisambhuṇanto vāti taṃ paṭipattiṃ asampādento vā.

'By the cutting off by another' means being prevented by another. 'Not being able to accomplish' means not fulfilling that practice.

Aññāya aparaddhoti nibbānena parihīno maggato vā. Taṃ vā satthaṃ anubandhatīti taṃ vā satthaṃ sabbattha pacchato gacchati.

'Having transgressed against final knowledge' means being deprived of Nibbāna or fallen from the path. 'He follows that caravan' means he follows that caravan everywhere, going behind it.

135. Evaṃ pana sīluttamānaṃ pavedhanakāraṇaṃ ariyasāvako sīlabbataṃ vāpi pahāya sabbanti gāthā. Tattha sāvajjānavajjanti sabbākusalaṃ lokiyakusalañca. Etaṃ suddhiṃ asuddhinti [P 2.0367] apatthayānoti pañcakāmaguṇādibhedaṃ suddhiṃ akusalādibhedaṃ asuddhiñca apatthayamāno. Virato careti suddhiyā asuddhiyā ca virato careyya. Santi manuggahāyāti diṭṭhiṃ aggahetvā.

135. Thus, the noble disciple, having abandoned all observances and practices that are a cause of agitation for those who hold virtue as supreme—this is the verse. Herein, 'blameworthy and blameless' refers to all that is unwholesome and all worldly wholesome actions. 'Not desiring this purity and impurity' means not desiring purity of the kinds such as the five strands of sensual pleasure, nor impurity of the kinds such as unwholesomeness. 'He would live detached' means he should live detached from purity and impurity. 'For the sake of peace' means not grasping views.

Kaṇhaṃ [V 0.0297] kaṇhavipākanti akusalakammaṃ akusalavipākadāyakaṃ. Sukkaṃ sukkavipākanti lokiyakusalaṃ attanā sadisaṃ sukkavipākadāyakaṃ.

'Dark with dark results' refers to unwholesome kamma that yields unwholesome results. 'Bright with bright results' refers to worldly wholesome kamma that yields bright results similar to itself.

Niyāmāvakkantinti maggapavisanaṃ. Sekkhāti satta sekkhā. Aggadhammanti uttamadhammaṃ, arahattaphalaṃ.

'Entering the fixed course' means entering the path. 'Trainee' means the seven trainees. 'Supreme Dhamma' means the highest Dhamma, the fruit of Arahantship.

136. Evaṃ ito bāhirake sīluttame saṃyamena visuddhivāde tesañca vipākaṃ sīlabbatapahāyino arahato ca paṭipattiṃ dassetvā idāni aññathāpi suddhivāde bāhirake dassento “tamūpanissāyā”ti gāthamāha. Tassattho – santaññepi samaṇabrāhmaṇā, te jigucchitaṃ amarantapaṃ vā diṭṭhasuddhiādīsu vā aññataraññataraṃ upanissāyaakiriyadiṭṭhiyā vā uddhaṃsarā hutvā bhavābhavesu avītataṇhā suddhi’manutthunanti vadanti kathentīti.

136. Having thus shown the external claims of purity through restraint based on the supremacy of virtue, their results, and the practice of the Arahant who has abandoned observances and practices, now, to show external claims of purity in another way, he speaks the verse beginning, 'Relying on that.' Its meaning is this: there are other ascetics and brahmins who, relying on some abhorrent austerity, or on one or another of the purifications by view and so on, or on the view of non-action, having become those who flow upwards, with craving for existence after existence unabandoned, praise, declare, and proclaim purity.

Tapojigucchavādāti kāyapīḷanāditapena pāpahirīyanavādā. Tapojigucchasārāti teneva tapena hirīyanasāravanto. Uddhaṃsarāvādāti saṃsārena suddhiṃ kathayantā.

'Those who teach austerity and scrupulousness' refers to those who teach being scrupulous about evil through austerity involving bodily torment and the like. 'Those for whom austerity and scrupulousness are the essence' means those who have scrupulousness as their essence due to that very austerity. 'Those who teach of flowing upwards' means those who declare purity through transmigration.

137. Evaṃ [M 0.0323] tesaṃ avītataṇhānaṃ suddhiṃ anutthunantānaṃ yopi suddhippattameva attānaṃ maññeyya, tassāpi avītataṇhattā bhavābhavesu taṃ taṃ vatthuṃ patthayamānassa hi jappitāni punappunaṃ hontiyevāti adhippāyo. Taṇhā hi āsevitā taṇhaṃ vaḍḍhayateva, na kevalañca jappitāni, pavedhitaṃ vāpi pakappitesu, taṇhādiṭṭhīhi cassa pakappitesu vatthūsu pavedhitampi hotīti vuttaṃ hoti. Bhavābhavesu pana vītataṇhattā āyatiṃ cutūpapāto idha yassa natthi, sa kena vedheyya kuhiṃ va jappeti ayametissā gāthāya sambandho.

137. Thus, even if one among those with unabandoned craving who praise purity were to consider oneself as having attained purity, for that one too, because their craving is unabandoned, while desiring various objects in one existence after another, their mutterings would indeed occur again and again—this is the meaning. For craving, when indulged, only increases craving. And not only mutterings, but there is also agitation regarding what is imagined; and due to craving and views, agitation also arises concerning imagined objects—this is what is said. However, for one free from craving for one existence after another, for whom there is no future passing away and rebirth here, by what could they be shaken? Where would they mutter? This is the connection of this verse.

Āgamananti puna āgamanaṃ. Gamananti ito aññattha gamanaṃ[P 2.0368]. Gamanāgamananti ito gantvā puna nivattanaṃ. Kālanti maraṇaṃ. Gatīti gamanavasena gatiyā gantabbaṃ.

'Coming' means coming again. 'Going' means going elsewhere from here. 'Going and coming' means going from here and then returning again. 'Time' means death. 'Destination' means that which is to be reached by way of going.

138. Yamāhu dhammanti pucchāgāthā.

138. 'That which they call Dhamma'—this is a question verse.

139. Idāni yasmā ekopi ettha vādo sacco natthi, kevalaṃ diṭṭhimattakena hi te vadanti, tasmā tamatthaṃ dassento “sakaṃ hī”ti imaṃ tāva vissajjanagāthamāha. Tattha sammutinti diṭṭhiṃ. Anomanti anūnaṃ.

139. Now, since not even one doctrine here is true—for they speak merely based on their own views—therefore, to explain that point, he first states this reply-verse, beginning: 'For his own...' Herein, 'convention' means view. 'Not inferior' means not deficient.

140. Evametesu [V 0.0298] sakaṃ dhammaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ brūvantesu aññassa dhammaṃ pana hīnanti vadantesu yassa kassaci – parassa ce vambhayitena hīnoti gāthā. Tassattho – yadi parassa ninditakāraṇā hīno bhaveyya, na koci dhammesu visesi aggo bhaveyya. Kiṃkāraṇā? Puthū hi aññassa vadanti dhammaṃ nihīnato sabbeva te samhi daḷhaṃ vadānāsakadhamme daḷhavādā eva.

140. Thus, while they declare their own doctrine as complete and another's doctrine as inferior, for anyone—'If by another's disparagement one is inferior' is the verse. Its meaning is this: if one were inferior due to being disparaged by another, then no doctrine would be special or supreme among doctrines. For what reason? Because many indeed declare another's doctrine to be inferior; all of them, speaking firmly of their own, are simply firm proponents of their own doctrine.

Vambhayitakāraṇāti dhaṃsitakāraṇā. Garahitakāraṇāti lāmakakatakāraṇā. Upavaditakāraṇāti akkositakāraṇā. Sakāyananti sakamaggaṃ.

'Because of being disparaged' means because of being scorned. 'Because of being blamed' means because of being made inferior. 'Because of being reproached' means because of being reviled. 'One's own way' means one's own path.

141. Kiñca bhiyyo – saddhammapūjāti gāthā. Tassattho – te ca titthiyā yathā pasaṃsanti sakāyanāni, saddhammapūjāpi nesaṃ tatheva vattati. Te hi ativiya satthārādīni sattaronti. Tattha yadi te pamāṇā siyuṃ, evaṃ sante sabbeva vādā tathiyā bhaveyyuṃ. Kiṃkāraṇā[M 0.0324]? Suddhī hi nesaṃ paccattameva. Na sā aññattha sijjhati, nāpi paramatthato. Attani diṭṭhigāhamattameva hi taṃ tesaṃ parapaccayaneyyabuddhīnaṃ. Paccattamevāti pāṭekkameva.

141. And what more? 'The praise of the good Dhamma'—this is a verse. Its meaning is this: Just as those sectarians praise their own ways, so too does their praise of their own good Dhamma proceed. They indeed excessively revere their own teachers and so on. If they were the standard, then all doctrines would be true. For what reason? Because their purity is merely personal. It is not accomplished elsewhere, nor in an ultimate sense. For them, whose intelligence is to be led by others, it is merely the grasping of a view in themselves. 'Paccattameva' means individually.

142. Yo pana viparītato bāhitapāpattā brāhmaṇo, tassa na brāhmaṇassa paraneyyamatthīti gāthā. Tassattho – brāhmaṇassa hi “sabbe saṅkhārā aniccā”tiādinā nayena sudiṭṭhattā parena netabbaṃ ñāṇaṃ natthi. Diṭṭhidhammesu “idameva [P 2.0369] sacca”nti nicchinitvā sumaggahītampi natthi. Taṃkāraṇā so diṭṭhikalahāni atikkanto, na hi so seṭṭhato passati dhammamaññaṃ aññatra satipaṭṭhānādīhi.

142. But for the brahmin who, contrary to this, has abandoned evil, for that brahmin there is nothing to be led to by another—this is the verse. Its meaning is this: For a brahmin, because he has seen well in the manner of 'All formations are impermanent,' and so on, there is no knowledge that he must be led to by another. Among doctrines, there is nothing firmly grasped after having decided, 'This alone is true.' For this reason, he has transcended disputes about views, and he does not see any other teaching as superior, apart from the foundations of mindfulness and the like.

Na paraneyyoti parena netabbo jānāpetabbo na hoti. Na parapattiyo na parapaccayoti paresaṃ paccetabbo na hoti. Na parapaṭibaddhagūti paresaṃ paṭibaddhagamano na hoti.

'Not to be led by another' (na paraneyyo) means he is not to be led or made to know by another. 'Not trusting in others, not conditioned by others' (na parapattiyo na parapaccayo) means he is not to be convinced by others. 'Not one whose going is tied to others' (na parapaṭibaddhagū) means he is not one whose going is bound to others.

143. Jānāmīti gāthāya sambandho attho ca – evaṃ tāva paramatthabrāhmaṇo na hi seṭṭhato passati dhammamaññaṃ, aññe pana titthiyā paracittañāṇādīhi jānantāpi passantāpi “jānāmi passāmi tatheva eta”nti evaṃ vadantāpi ca diṭṭhiyā suddhiṃ paccenti. Kasmā? Yasmā tesu ekopi adakkhi ce addasa cepi tena paracittañāṇādinā yathābhūtamatthaṃ, kiñhi tumassa tena tassa tena dassanena kiṃ kataṃ, kiṃ dukkhapariññā sādhitā, udāhu samudayappahānādīnaṃ aññataraṃ, yato sabbathāpi atikkamitvā ariyamaggaṃ te titthiyā aññeneva [V 0.0299] vadanti suddhiṃ, atikkamitvā vā te titthiye buddhādayo aññeneva vadanti suddhinti.

143. The connection and meaning of the verse beginning 'I know' is as follows: Thus, the ultimate Brahmin does not see any other teaching as superior. But other sectarians, even while knowing and seeing with powers such as knowledge of others' minds, and even while saying, 'I know, I see, it is just so,' still rely on their views for purity. Why? Because even if one among them saw—even if he saw the meaning as it really is with that knowledge of others' minds and so on—what has been accomplished for him by that seeing? Has the full understanding of suffering been achieved? Or has one of the tasks, such as the abandoning of the origin, been achieved? Since in every way, having bypassed the Noble Path, those sectarians declare purity by other means; or, having surpassed those sectarians, the Buddhas and others declare purity by other means.

144. Passaṃ naroti gāthāya sambandho attho ca – kiñca bhiyyo? Yvāyaṃ paracittañāṇādīhi addakkhi, so passaṃ naro dakkhati nāmarūpaṃ, na tato paraṃ, disvāna vā ñassati tānimeva nāmarūpāni niccato sukhato vā, na aññathā; so evaṃ passanto kāmaṃ bahuṃ passatu appakaṃ vā nāmarūpaṃ niccato sukhato ca athassa evarūpena dassanena na hi tena suddhiṃ kusalā vadanti.

144. The connection and meaning of the verse beginning 'A seeing person' is as follows: And what more? Whoever sees with knowledge of others' minds and so on, that seeing person sees name-and-form, and nothing beyond. And having seen, he will know that very name-and-form as permanent or as pleasant, but not otherwise. Let him, seeing thus, see as he wishes much or little name-and-form as permanent and pleasant; yet the skillful do not say that purity comes from such seeing.

145. Nivissavādīti [M 0.0325] gāthāya sambandho attho ca – tena ca dassanena suddhiyā asatiyāpi yo “jānāmi passāmi tatheva eta”nti evaṃ nivissavādī, etaṃ vā dassanaṃ paṭicca diṭṭhiyā suddhiṃ paccento “idameva sacca”nti evaṃ nivissavādī, so subbinayo na hoti taṃ tathā pakappitaṃ abhisaṅkhataṃ diṭṭhiṃ purakkharāno. So hi yaṃ satthārādiṃ nissito, tattheva subhaṃ vadāno suddhiṃ vado, “parisuddhivādo [P 2.0370] parisuddhidassano vā aha”nti attānaṃ maññamāno tattha tathaddasā so, tattha sakāya diṭṭhiyā aviparītameva so addasa. Yathā sā diṭṭhi pavattati, tatheva taṃ addasa, na aññathā passituṃ icchatīti adhippāyo.

145. The connection and meaning of the verse 'Nivissavādī' is as follows: Even though there is no purity through that seeing, one who declares, 'I know, I see, it is exactly so,' is thus one who speaks with insistence. Alternatively, one who, relying on that seeing, proclaims purity by means of a view, saying, 'This alone is true,' is also one who speaks with insistence. Such a person is not easy to guide, for they uphold that fabricated, constructed view. Indeed, whoever relies on a teacher or the like, proclaiming the auspiciousness thereof and proclaiming purity therein, considering themselves as 'one who proclaims purity or sees purity,' sees accordingly there. There, they see only what is consistent with their own view; they see it exactly as that view operates, not desiring to see otherwise—this is the intended meaning.

Nivissavādīti patiṭṭhahitvā kathento. Dubbinayoti vinetuṃ dukkho. Duppaññāpayoti ñāpetuṃ cittena labbhāpetuṃ dukkho. Dunnijjhāpayoti cittena vīmaṃsitvā gahaṇatthaṃ punappunaṃ nijjhāpayituṃ dukkho. Duppekkhāpayoti ikkhāpayituṃ dukkho. Duppasādayoti citte pasādaṃ uppādetuṃ dukkho.

'Nivissavādī' means one who speaks after taking a stand. 'Dubbinayo' means difficult to train. 'Duppaññāpayo' means difficult to make understand or to inform. 'Dunnijjhāpayo' means difficult to cause to repeatedly examine mentally in order to grasp the meaning. 'Duppekkhāpayo' means difficult to make see. 'Duppasādayo' means difficult to produce confidence in the mind.

Appassīti ñāṇena paṭivedhaṃ pāpuṇi. Paṭivijjhīti cittena avabodhaṃ pāpuṇi.

'Appassī' means one who attained penetration by knowledge. 'Paṭivijjhī' means one who attained understanding by the mind.

146. Evaṃ pakappitaṃ diṭṭhiṃ purakkharānesu titthiyesu – na brāhmaṇo kappamupeti saṅkhāti gāthā. Tattha saṅkhāti saṅkhāya, jānitvāti attho. Napi ñāṇabandhūti samāpattiñāṇādinā akatataṇhādiṭṭhibandhu. Tattha viggaho – nāpi assa ñāṇena kato bandhu atthīti napi ñāṇabandhu. Sammutiyoti diṭṭhisammutiyo. Puthujjāti puthujjanasambhavā. Uggahaṇanti maññeti uggahaṇanti aññe, aññe tā sammutiyo uggaṇhantīti vuttaṃ hoti.

146. Among the sectarians who prioritize such fabricated views—the verse states, 'No brahmin resorts to reckoning.' Here, 'saṅkhāti' means by reckoning, that is, by knowing. 'Nor is he bound by knowledge' (napi ñāṇabandhu) means he is not bound by craving and wrong views through the knowledge of attainments and so forth. The analysis here is: nor is there a bond made for him by knowledge, thus 'napi ñāṇabandhu.' 'Sammutiyo' refers to conventional views. 'Puthujjāti' means originating from worldlings. 'Uggahaṇanti' means they suppose—some say, 'they grasp,' meaning it is said that others grasp those conventions.

Upekkhatīti [V 0.0300] upapattito apakkhapatito hutvā passati.

'Upekkhati' means seeing impartially, without siding with any form of existence.

147. Kiñca bhiyyo – vissajja ganthānīti gāthā. Tattha anuggahoti uggahaṇavirahito, sopi nāssa uggahoti anuggaho. Na vā uggaṇhātīti anuggaho.

147. What more? – The verse states, 'having released the knots.' Here, 'anuggaho' means devoid of grasping; that is, there is no grasping for him, thus 'anuggaho.' Or, it means he does not grasp, hence 'anuggaho.'

Ganthe vossajjitvāti abhijjhādike ganthe cajitvā. Vissajjāti puna anādiyanavasena jahitvā. Gadhiteti ghaṭite. Ganthiteti suttena saṅgahite viya ganthite. Bandheti suṭṭhu bandhe. Vibandheti vividhā bandhe. Palibuddheti [M 0.0326] samantato bandhanena bandhe. Bandhaneti kilesabandhane. Phoṭayitvāti papphoṭetvā. Saccaṃ vissajjaṃ karontīti visaṅkharitvā aparibhogaṃ karonti. Vikopentīti cuṇṇavicuṇṇaṃ karonti.

'Ganthe vossajjitvā' means having abandoned the knots of covetousness and so forth. 'Vissajjāti' means having abandoned by way of not taking up again. 'Gadhite' means clung to. 'Ganthite' means bound, as if held together with thread. 'Bandheti' means firmly binds. 'Vibandheti' means binds in diverse ways. 'Palibuddheti' means completely bound by bonds. 'Bandhane' refers to the bondage of defilements. 'Phoṭayitvā' means having burst. 'Saccaṃ vissajjaṃ karonti' means having deconstructed, they render it unusable. 'Vikopenti' means they reduce it to dust.

148. Kiñca bhiyyo – so evarūpo – pubbāsaveti gāthā. Tattha pubbāsaveti atītarūpādīni ārabbha uppajjanadhammakilese[P 2.0371]. Naveti paccuppannarūpādīni ārabbha uppajjanadhamme. Na chandagūti chandādivasena na gacchati. Anattagarahīti katākatavasena attānaṃ agarahanto.

148. What more? – Such a one – the verse states, 'former taints.' Herein, 'former taints' (pubbāsava) refers to defilements that tend to arise concerning past forms and so forth. 'New' (nava) refers to defilements that tend to arise concerning present forms and so forth. 'Not led by desire' (Na chandagū) means not proceeding based on desire and so forth. 'Not blaming the self' (Anattagarahī) means not blaming oneself on account of what has or has not been done.

149. Evaṃ anattagarahī ca – sa sabbadhammesūti gāthā. Tattha sabbadhammesūti dvāsaṭṭhidiṭṭhidhammesu “yaṃ kiñci diṭṭhaṃ vā”ti evaṃpabhedesu. Pannabhāroti patitabhāro. Na kappetīti na kappiyo, duvidhampi kappaṃ na karotīti attho. Nūparatoti puthujjanakalyāṇakasekkhā viya uparatisamaṅgīpi no hoti. Na patthiyoti nittaṇho. Taṇhā hi patthayatīti patthiyā, nāssa patthiyāti na patthiyo. Ito parañca heṭṭhā ca tattha tattha vuttanayattā uttānatthameva. Evaṃ arahattanikūṭeneva desanaṃ niṭṭhāpesi, desanāpariyosāne purābhedasutte (mahāni. 83) vuttasadiso eva abhisamayo ahosīti.

149. Thus, not blaming the self – the verse states, 'He, in all things...' Herein, 'in all things' refers to the sixty-two kinds of speculative views, in such divisions as 'whatever is seen,' etc. 'With burden dropped' (pannabhāro) means the burden is cast off. 'He does not form conceptions' (na kappeti) means he is not one who forms conceptions; that is, he does not engage in either kind of fabrication. 'Not ceased' (nūparato) means he is not endowed with cessation like ordinary people, virtuous commoners, or trainees. 'Not longing' (na patthiyo) means without craving. For craving longs, thus it is called 'longing'; he has no longing, thus he is 'not longing.' Beyond this and below, the meaning is clear according to the method stated here and there. Thus, the teaching was concluded at the peak of arahantship, and at the end of the teaching, a realization occurred similar to that stated in the Purābheda Sutta (Mahāni. 83).

Saddhammappajjotikāya mahāniddesaṭṭhakathāya

From the Saddhammappajjotikā, the Commentary on the Mahāniddesa.

Mahābyūhasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Exposition of the Mahābyūha Sutta is concluded.

14. Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesavaṇṇanā

14. The Commentary on the Exposition of the Tuvaṭaka Sutta

150. Cuddasame [V 0.0301][P 2.0372] tuvaṭakasuttaniddese pucchāmi tanti idampi tasmiṃyeva mahāsamaye “kā nu kho arahattappattiyā paṭipattī”ti uppannacittānaṃ ekaccānaṃ devatānaṃ tamatthaṃ pakāsetuṃ purimanayeneva nimmitabuddhena attānaṃ pucchāpetvā vuttaṃ.

150. In the fourteenth, the Exposition of the Tuvaṭaka Sutta, the phrase 'I ask you'—this too was spoken at that same great assembly. For some deities, the thought had arisen, 'What, indeed, is the practice for the attainment of arahantship?' In order to reveal that meaning to them, a created Buddha had himself questioned, in the same manner as before.

Tattha ādipucchāgāthāya tāva pucchāmīti ettha adiṭṭhajotanādivasena pucchā vibhajitā. Ādiccabandhūti ādiccassa gottabandhu. Vivekaṃ [M 0.0327] santipadañcāti vivekañca santipadañca. Kathaṃ disvāti kena kāraṇena disvā, kathaṃ pavattadassano hutvāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Herein, first, in the initial question verse, regarding the phrase 'I ask,' the question is analyzed by way of 'unseen illumination' and so forth. 'Kinsman of the Sun' means a kinsman of the solar lineage. 'Detachment and the peaceful state' means detachment and also the peaceful state. 'Having seen how' means 'having seen for what reason'; that is to say, 'having become one who sees how it proceeds.'

Tisso pucchāti gaṇanaparicchedo. Adiṭṭhajotanāti yaṃ na diṭṭhaṃ na paṭividdhaṃ, tassa pākaṭakaraṇatthāya pucchā. Diṭṭhasaṃsandanāti yaṃ ñāṇacakkhunā diṭṭhaṃ, tassa ghaṭanatthāya. Vimaticchedanāti yā kaṅkhā, tassācchedanatthaṃ. Pakatiyā lakkhaṇaṃ aññātanti dhammānaṃ tathalakkhaṇaṃ pakatiyā na ñātaṃ. Adiṭṭhanti na diṭṭhaṃ. “Na niṭṭha”ntipi pāṭho. Atulitanti tulāya tulitaṃ viya na tulitaṃ. Atīritanti tīraṇāya na tīritaṃ. Avibhūtanti na pākaṭaṃ. Avibhāvitanti paññāya na vaḍḍhitaṃ. Tassa ñāṇāyāti tassa dhammassa lakkhaṇajānanatthāya. Dassanāyāti dassanatthāya. Tulanāyāti tulanatthāya. Tīraṇāyāti tīraṇatthāya. Vibhāvanāyāti vibhāgakaraṇatthāya. Aññehi paṇḍitehīti aññehi buddhisampannehi. Saṃsayapakkhandoti sandehaṃ paviṭṭho.

'Three questions' is a specification of the number. 'Unseen illumination' means a question for the purpose of making manifest that which has not been seen or penetrated. 'Confirmation of what is seen' means for the purpose of connecting that which has been seen with the eye of wisdom. 'Cutting off doubt' means for the purpose of cutting off whatever uncertainty there is. 'By nature, the characteristic is unknown' means the true characteristic of phenomena is not known by nature. 'Unseen' means not seen. 'Not concluded' is also a reading. 'Not weighed' means not weighed as if by a scale. 'Not examined' means not examined by investigation. 'Not revealed' means not manifest. 'Not developed' means not developed by wisdom. 'For the sake of knowing it' means for the purpose of knowing the characteristic of that phenomenon. 'For the sake of seeing' means for the purpose of seeing. 'For the sake of weighing' means for the purpose of weighing. 'For the sake of examining' means for the purpose of examining. 'For the sake of clarifying' means for the purpose of making distinctions. 'By other wise ones' means by others endowed with intelligence. 'Leaping into doubt' means having entered into doubt.

Manussapucchāti manussānaṃ pucchā. Amanussapucchāti nāgasupaṇṇādīnaṃ pucchā. Gahaṭṭhāti avasesagahaṭṭhā. Pabbajitāti liṅgavasena vuttā. Nāgāti suphassādayo nāgā. Supaṇṇāti supaṇṇasaṃyuttavasena (saṃ. ni. 3.392 ādayo). Yakkhāti yakkhasaṃyuttavasena (saṃ. ni. 10.235 ādayo) ca veditabbā[P 2.0373]. Asurāti pahārādādayo. Gandhabbāti pañcasikhagandhabbaputtādayo[V 0.0302]. Mahārājānoti cattāro mahārājāno. Ahīnindriyanti saṇṭhānavasena avikalindriyaṃ. So nimmitoti so bhagavatā nimmito buddho.

'A question from humans' means a question of humans. 'A question from non-humans' means a question of nāgas, supaṇṇas, and so on. 'Householders' means the remaining householders. 'Renunciants' is stated in terms of outward form. 'Nāgas' refers to nāgas such as Suphassa and so on. 'Supaṇṇas' should be understood in accordance with the Supaṇṇa Saṃyutta (SN 3.392 onwards). 'Yakkhas' should be understood in accordance with the Yakkha Saṃyutta (SN 10.235 onwards). 'Asuras' refers to those such as Pahārāda and so on. 'Gandhabbas' refers to gandhabba sons such as Pañcasikha and so on. 'Great Kings' refers to the four Great Kings. 'With unimpaired faculties' means having faculties that are complete in their form, not deficient. 'He who was created' means that Buddha was created by the Blessed One.

Vodānatthapucchāti visesadhammapucchā. Atītapucchāti atīte dhamme ārabbha pucchā. Anāgatādīsupi eseva nayo. Kusalapucchāti anavajjadhammapucchā. Akusalapucchāti sāvajjadhammapucchā. Abyākatapucchāti tadubhayaviparītadhammapucchā.

A question for the sake of purification is a question about special phenomena. A question about the past is a question concerning past phenomena. The same method applies to the future and so on. A question about the skillful is a question about blameless phenomena. A question about the unskillful is a question about blameworthy phenomena. A question about the indeterminate is a question about phenomena contrary to both.

Ajjhesāmi tanti taṃ āṇāpemi. Kathayassu meti mayhaṃ kathehi. Gottañātakoti gottena ñātako. Gottabandhūti gottajjhattiko. Ekenākārenāti ekena koṭṭhāsena.

'I request you' means 'I command you.' 'Speak to me' means 'tell it to me.' 'Known by clan' means 'a relative by clan.' 'A clan relative' means 'one belonging to the clan.' 'In one manner' means 'in one section.'

Santipadanti santisaṅkhātaṃ nibbānapadaṃ. Ye dhammā santādhigamāyāti ye satipaṭṭhānādayo dhammā nibbānapaṭilābhatthāya. Santiphusanāyāti ñāṇaphassena [M 0.0328] nibbānaphusanatthāya. Sacchikiriyāyāti paccakkhakaraṇatthāya. Mahantaṃ sīlakkhandhanti mahantaṃ sīlarāsiṃ. Samādhikkhandhādīsupi eseva nayo. Sīlakkhandhādayo lokiyalokuttarā, vimuttiñāṇadassanaṃ lokiyameva.

'The peaceful state' means the state of Nibbāna, which is called peace. 'Those phenomena that lead to the attainment of peace' means those phenomena, such as the foundations of mindfulness and so forth, are for the purpose of attaining Nibbāna. 'For the sake of touching peace' means for the purpose of touching Nibbāna through the touch of knowledge. 'For the sake of realization' means for the purpose of direct realization. 'The great aggregate of virtue' means the great mass of virtue. The same method applies to the aggregates of concentration and so forth. The aggregates of virtue and so forth are mundane or supramundane, but the knowledge and vision of liberation is solely mundane.

Tamokāyassa padālananti avijjārāsissa viddhaṃsanaṃ. Vipallāsassa bhedananti catubbidhavipallāsassa bhedanaṃ. Taṇhāsallassa abbuhananti taṇhākaṇṭakassa luñcanaṃ. Abhisaṅkhārassa vūpasamanti puññādiabhisaṅkhārassa nibbāpanaṃ. Bhārassa nikkhepananti pañcakkhandhabhārassa ṭhapanaṃ. Saṃsāravaṭṭassa upacchedananti saṃsārapavattassa chedanaṃ. Santāpassa nibbāpananti kilesasantāpassa nibbuti. Pariḷāhassa paṭipassaddhinti kilesadarathassa sannisīdanaṃ. Devadevoti devānaṃ atidevo.

'The destruction of the mass of darkness' means the demolition of the heap of ignorance. 'The breaking of distortion' means the breaking of the four kinds of distortion. 'The plucking out of the dart of craving' means the uprooting of the thorn of craving. 'The calming of volitional formations' means the extinguishing of meritorious and other volitional formations. 'The laying down of the burden' means the abandonment of the burden of the five aggregates. 'The cutting off of the cycle of existence' means the cutting off of the turning of saṃsāra. 'The quenching of torment' means the extinguishing of the torment of defilements. 'The pacification of anguish' means the subsiding of the burning of defilements. 'The god of gods' means the supreme god of gods.

151. Atha bhagavā yasmā yathā passanto kilese uparundhati, tathā disvā tathā pavattadassano hutvā parinibbāti, tasmā tamatthaṃ āvikaronto nānappakārena taṃ devaparisaṃ kilesappahāne [P 2.0374] niyojento “mūlaṃ papañcasaṅkhāyā”ti ārabhitvā pañca gāthā abhāsi.

151. Then, because the Blessed One obstructs the defilements by seeing in a certain way, and having thus seen and become one whose vision proceeds in that way, attains final Nibbāna, therefore, making that meaning clear and in various ways engaging that assembly of gods in the abandoning of defilements, he began with 'The root of conceptual proliferation' and spoke five verses.

Tattha ādigāthāya tāva saṅkhepattho – papañcasaṅkhāti papañcāti saṅkhātattā papañcā eva papañcasaṅkhā. Tassā avijjādayo kilesā mūlaṃ, taṃ papañcasaṅkhāya mūlaṃ asmīti pavattamānañca [V 0.0303] sabbaṃ mantāya uparundhe. Yā kāci ajjhattaṃ taṇhā uppajjeyyuṃ. Tāsaṃ vinayāya pahānāya sadā sato sikkhe upaṭṭhitassati hutvā sikkheyyāti.

Here, the meaning of the first verse in brief is: `Papañcasaṅkhā` means proliferations themselves, so called because they are designated as 'proliferation.' Its root is the defilements beginning with ignorance. That root of conceptual proliferation, and all that proceeds as 'I am,' one should obstruct by wisdom. Whatever cravings might arise internally, for their removal and abandonment, one should always train mindfully, having become one with established mindfulness.

Ajjhattasamuṭṭhānā vāti citte uppannā vā. Purebhattanti divābhattato purekālaṃ. Accantasaṃyogatthe upayogavacanaṃ, atthato pana bhummameva purebhatteti, esa nayo pacchābhattādīsu. Pacchābhattanti divābhattato pacchākālaṃ. Purimaṃ yāmanti rattiyā paṭhamakoṭṭhāsaṃ. Majjhimaṃ yāmanti rattiyā dutiyakoṭṭhāsaṃ. Pacchimaṃ yāmanti rattiyā tatiyakoṭṭhāsaṃ. Kāḷeti kāḷapakkhe. Juṇheti sukkapakkhe. Vasseti cattāro vassānamāse. Hemanteti cattāro hemantamāse. Gimheti cattāro gimhānamāse. Purime vayokhandheti paṭhame vayokoṭṭhāse, paṭhamavayeti attho. Tīsu ca vayesu vassasatāyukassa purisassa ekekasmiṃ vaye catumāsādhikāni tettiṃsa vassāni honti.

'Arising internally' means arising in the mind. 'Before the meal' means the time before the midday meal. The word is in the accusative case in the sense of continuous connection, but in meaning, 'before the meal' is simply in the locative. This same method applies to 'after the meal' and so on. 'After the meal' means the time after the midday meal. 'The first watch' means the first portion of the night. 'The middle watch' means the second portion of the night. 'The last watch' means the third portion of the night. 'In the dark fortnight' means in the dark fortnight. 'In the bright fortnight' means in the bright fortnight. 'In the rainy season' means the four months of the rainy season. 'In the winter season' means the four months of the cold season. 'In the hot season' means the four months of the hot season. 'In the first age division' means in the first portion of life, that is, the first age. And in the three ages, for a person with a lifespan of one hundred years, in each age there are thirty-three years and four months.

152. Evaṃ [M 0.0329] paṭhamagāthāya tāva tīhi sikkhāhi yuttaṃ desanaṃ arahattanikūṭena desetvā puna mānappahānavasena desetuṃ “yaṃ kiñcī”ti gāthamāha. Tattha yaṃ kiñci dhammamabhijaññā ajjhattanti yaṃ kiñci uccākulīnatādikaṃ attano guṇaṃ jāneyya. Atha vāpi bahiddhāti atha vā bahiddhāpi ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ vā guṇaṃ jāneyya. Na tena thāmaṃ kubbethāti tena guṇena mānaṃ na kareyya.

152. Thus, having first explained the teaching connected with the three trainings, with arahantship as its pinnacle, through the initial verse, and in order to teach further by way of the abandonment of conceit, he spoke the verse 'Yaṃ kiñcī.' Herein, 'whatever quality one may know within oneself' refers to knowing any quality of one's own, such as high birth and the like. Or else, 'or outside' means knowing the qualities of teachers or preceptors outside oneself. 'One should not be proud because of it' means one should not make conceit because of that quality.

Satānanti santaguṇavantānaṃ. Santānanti nibbutasantānaṃ. Na vuttāti na kathitā. Nappavuttāti na vissajjitā.

'Of the peaceful' means of those endowed with peaceful qualities. 'Of the peaceful ones' means of those whose minds are extinguished and calmed. 'Not spoken' means not said. 'Not declared' means not uttered.

153. Idānissa akaraṇavidhiṃ dassento “seyyo na tenā”ti gāthamāha. Tassattho – tena ca mānena “seyyoha”nti vā “nīcoha”nti [P 2.0375] vā “sarikkhoha”nti vāpi na maññeyya. Tehi ca uccākulīnatādīhi guṇehi phuṭṭho anekarūpehi “ahaṃ uccā kulā pabbajito”tiādinā nayena attānaṃ vikappento na tiṭṭheyyāti.

153. Now, showing the method of not doing this, he spoke the verse 'Seyyo na tenā.' Its meaning is: one should not think 'I am better,' 'I am inferior,' or even 'I am equal' because of that conceit. And being touched by those qualities such as high birth and the like in various ways, one should not remain conceiving of oneself in ways such as, 'I have gone forth from a high family,' and so on.

154. Evaṃ mānappahānavasenapi desetvā idāni sabbakilesūpasamavasena desetuṃ “ajjhattamevā”ti gāthamāha. Tattha ajjhattamevupasameti attani eva rāgādisabbakilese upasameyya. Na aññato bhikkhu santimeseyyāti ṭhapetvā ca satipaṭṭhānādīni aññena upāyena santiṃ na pariyeseyya. Kuto nirattā vāti nirattā kutoyeva.

154. Having thus taught by way of the abandonment of conceit, now, in order to teach by way of the calming of all defilements, he speaks the verse 'Ajjhattameva.' Therein, 'one should calm within oneself' means one should calm all defilements such as lust within oneself alone. 'A bhikkhu should not seek serenity from elsewhere' means that, setting aside the foundations of mindfulness and so forth, one should not seek serenity by any other means. 'From where, for one without self?' means 'for one who is without self, from where else?'

Na [V 0.0304] eseyyāti sīlabbatādīhi na maggeyya. Na gaveseyyāti na olokeyya. Na pariyeseyyāti punappunaṃ na ikkheyya.

'One should not seek' means one should not pursue through vows and practices and so forth. 'One should not search' means one should not look. 'One should not seek for' means one should not repeatedly observe.

155. Idāni ajjhattaṃ upasantassa khīṇāsavassa tādibhāvaṃ dassento “majjhe yathā”ti gāthamāha. Tassattho – yathā mahāsamuddassa upariheṭṭhimabhāgānaṃ vemajjhasaṅkhāte catuyojanasahassappamāṇe majjhe pabbatantare ṭhitassa vā majjhe samuddassa ūmi no jāyati, ṭhitova so hoti avikampamāno, evaṃ anejo khīṇāsavo lābhādīsu ṭhito assa avikampamāno, so tādiso rāgādiussadaṃ bhikkhu na kareyya kuhiñcīti.

155. Now, showing the state of suchness of one who is inwardly calmed and whose taints are destroyed, he spoke the verse 'Majjhe yathā.' Its meaning is: just as in the great ocean—in the middle part, described as the intermediate area between the upper and lower parts, four thousand yojanas in extent, or in the middle of the ocean situated between mountains—no wave is born, and it remains still, unmoving; even so, the passionless one whose taints are destroyed, standing amidst gain and the like, should be unmoving. Such a bhikkhu should not create an elevation of lust and the like anywhere.

Ubbedhenāti heṭṭhābhāgena. Gambhīroti udakapiṭṭhito paṭṭhāya caturāsītiyojanasahassāni gambhīro. “Ubbedho”tipi pāṭho, taṃ na [M 0.0330] sundaraṃ. Heṭṭhāti antoudakaṃ. Uparīti uddhaṃudakaṃ. Majjheti vemajjhe. Na kampatīti ṭhitaṭṭhānato na calati. Na vikampatīti ito cito ca na calati. Na calatīti niccalaṃ hoti. Na vedhatīti na phandati. Nappavedhatīti na parivattati. Na sampavedhatīti na paribbhamati. Aneritoti na erito. Aghaṭṭitoti akkhobho. Acalitoti na kampito. Aluḷitoti na kalalībhūto. Tatra ūmi no jāyatīti tasmiṃ ṭhāne vīci na uppajjati.

By 'ubbedhena' is meant by the lower part. By 'gambhīro' is meant deep, being eighty-four thousand yojanas deep starting from the surface of the water. The reading 'ubbedho' is also found, but it is not good. By 'heṭṭhā' is meant the water within. By 'uparī' is meant the water above. By 'majjhe' is meant in the very middle. By 'na kampati' is meant it does not stir from its fixed position. By 'na vikampati' is meant it does not stir hither and thither. By 'na calati' is meant it is motionless. By 'na vedhati' is meant it does not tremble. By 'nappavedhati' is meant it does not revolve. By 'na sampavedhati' is meant it does not whirl around. By 'anerito' is meant not agitated. By 'aghaṭṭito' is meant undisturbed. By 'acalito' is meant unshaken. By 'aluḷito' is meant not muddied. By 'tatra ūmi no jāyati' is meant in that place a wave does not arise.

Sattannaṃ pabbatānaṃ antarikāsūti yugandharādīnaṃ sattannaṃ pabbatānaṃ antarantarā. Sīdantarāti antamaso simbalītūlampi tesu patitapatitaṃ sīdatīti sīdā, pabbatantare jātattā antarā. “Antarasīdā”tipi pāṭho.

By 'in the spaces of the seven mountains' is meant between each of the seven mountains such as Yugandhara and so forth. By 'sīdantarā' is meant that even kapok cotton, when it falls into them, sinks; hence they are 'sīdā' (sinks), and because they are born between the mountains, they are 'antarā' (between). The reading 'Antarasīdā' is also found.

156. Idāni [P 2.0376] evaṃ arahattanikūṭena desitaṃ dhammadesanaṃ abbhānumodento tassa ca arahattassa ādipaṭipadaṃ pucchanto nimmitabuddho “akittayī”ti gāthamāha. Tattha akittayīti ācikkhi. Vivaṭacakkhūti vivaṭehi anāvaraṇehi pañcahi cakkhūhi samannāgato. Sakkhidhammanti sakāyattaṃ sayaṃ abhiññātaṃ attapaccakkhadhammaṃ. Parissayavinayanti parissayavinayanaṃ. Paṭipadaṃ vadehīti idāni paṭipattiṃ vadehi. Bhaddanteti bhaddaṃ tava atthūti bhagavantaṃ ālapanto āha. Atha vā bhaddaṃ sundaraṃ tava paṭipadaṃ vadehītipi vuttaṃ hoti. Pātimokkhaṃ atha vāpi samādhinti tameva paṭipadaṃ bhinditvā pucchati. Paṭipadanti etena vā maggaṃ pucchati. Itarehi sīlaṃ samādhiñca pucchati.

156. Now, the created Buddha, rejoicing in the Dhamma teaching thus expounded by the pinnacle of arahantship and asking about the initial practice for that arahantship, spoke the verse 'akittayī.' Here, 'akittayī' means he declared. 'Vivaṭacakkhu' means endowed with the five unobstructed eyes. 'Sakkhidhamma' means the Dhamma that is one's own possession, directly known by oneself, personally experienced. 'Parissayavinayana' means the removal of dangers. 'Paṭipadaṃ vadehi' means 'now speak of the practice.' 'Bhaddante' means, addressing the Blessed One, he said, 'May there be good for you.' Alternatively, it is said, 'Speak of your beautiful practice.' 'Pātimokkhaṃ atha vāpi samādhiṃ' means he asks about that very practice by dividing it. By 'paṭipadaṃ' he asks about the path. By the others he asks about virtue and concentration.

Maṃsacakkhunāpīti [V 0.0305] sasambhārikamaṃsacakkhunāpi. Dibbacakkhunāpīti dibbasadisattā dibbaṃ. Devānañhi sucaritakammanibbattaṃ pittasemharuhirādīhi apalibuddhaṃ upakkilesavinimuttatāya dūrepi ārammaṇasampaṭicchanasamatthaṃ dibbaṃ pasādacakkhu hoti. Idañcāpi vīriyabhāvanābalanibbattaṃ ñāṇacakkhu tādisamevāti dibbasadisattā dibbaṃ. Dibbavihāravasena paṭiladdhattā, attanā ca dibbavihārasannissitattāpi dibbaṃ. Ālokapariggahena mahājutikattāpi dibbaṃ. Tirokuṭṭādigatarūpadassanena mahāgatikattāpi dibbaṃ. Taṃ sabbaṃ saddasatthānusārena veditabbaṃ. Dassanaṭṭhena cakkhu, cakkhukiccakaraṇena cakkhumivātipi cakkhu, dibbañca taṃ cakkhu cāti dibbacakkhu. Tena dibbacakkhunāpi vivaṭacakkhu. Idāni pañcavidhaṃ cakkhuṃ vitthārena kathetuṃ “kathaṃ bhagavā maṃsacakkhunāpi vivaṭacakkhū”tiādimāha[M 0.0331]. Maṃsacakkhumhi bhagavato pañcavaṇṇā saṃvijjantīti ettha sasambhārādikacakkhumhi buddhassa bhagavato pañca koṭṭhāsā paccekaṃ paccekaṃ upalabbhanti.

By 'maṃsacakkhunāpi' is meant even with the fleshly eye that depends on its constituents. By 'dibbacakkhunāpi' is meant 'divine' because it is similar to the divine. For the divine sensitive eye of deities is produced by their wholesome kamma, unobstructed by bile, phlegm, blood, and so forth, free from defilements, and capable of perceiving objects even from afar. And this eye of knowledge, produced by the power of energy and development, is also similar to that; hence, it is called divine because it is similar to the divine. It is also divine because it is attained through divine abidings, and because it itself relies on divine abidings. It is also divine due to its great radiance in grasping light. It is also divine due to its great range in seeing forms beyond walls and so forth. All this should be understood in accordance with the science of grammar. An eye is so called because it sees, and it is also an eye because it performs the function of an eye; and since it is divine and an eye, it is a divine eye. Even with that divine eye, the eye is open. Now, to explain the five kinds of eyes in detail, it is said, 'How is the Blessed One open-eyed even with the fleshly eye?' and so forth. Here, in the fleshly eye of the Blessed One, five colors are found. In the eye with its constituents and so forth, of the Buddha, the Blessed One, five parts are found individually.

Nīlo ca vaṇṇoti umāpupphavaṇṇo. Pītako ca vaṇṇoti kaṇikārapupphavaṇṇo. Lohitako ca vaṇṇoti indagopakavaṇṇo. Kaṇho ca vaṇṇoti añjanavaṇṇo. Odāto ca vaṇṇoti osadhitārakavaṇṇo. Yattha ca akkhilomāni patiṭṭhitānīti yasmiṃ ṭhāne akkhilomāni patiṭṭhahitvā [P 2.0377] uṭṭhitāni. Taṃ nīlaṃ hoti sunīlanti ettha nīlanti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ. Sunīlanti antaravirahitaṃ suṭṭhu nīlaṃ. Pāsādikanti pasādajanakaṃ. Dassaneyyanti dassanīyaṃ. Umāpupphasamānanti dakasītalapupphasadisaṃ. Tassa paratoti tassa samantā bāhirapasse. Pītakanti sabbasaṅgāhakaṃ. Supītakanti antaravirahitaṃ suṭṭhu pītakaṃ. Ubhayato ca akkhikūṭānīti dve ca akkhikoṭiyo. Lohitakānīti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ. Sulohitakānīti apaññāyamānavivarāni suṭṭhu lohitakāni. Majjhe kaṇhanti akkhīnaṃ majjhimaṭṭhānaṃ añjanasadisaṃ kaṇhaṃ. Sukaṇhanti antaravirahitaṃ suṭṭhu kaṇhaṃ. Alūkhanti pāsādikaṃ. Siniddhanti paṇītaṃ. Bhaddāriṭṭhakasamānanti apanītatacabhaddāriṭṭhakaphalasadisaṃ. “Addāriṭṭhakasamāna”ntipi pāḷi, tassā tintakākasadisanti attho. Odātanti sabbasaṅgāhakavasena vuttaṃ. Suodātanti antaravirahitaṃ rajatamaṇḍalasadisaṃ suṭṭhu odātaṃ. Setaṃ paṇḍaranti dvīhipi atiodātataṃ dasseti. Pākatikena maṃsacakkhunāti pakatimaṃsacakkhunā. Attabhāvapariyāpannenāti attabhāvasannissitena. Purimasucaritakammābhinibbattenāti purimesu tattha tatthuppannesu attabhāvesu kāyasucaritādikammunā uppāditena. Samantā yojanaṃ passatīti samantato catugāvutappamāṇe yojane tirokuṭṭādigataṃ rūpaṃ āvaraṇavirahitaṃ pakatimaṃsacakkhunā dakkhati.

The blue color is like the hue of the umā flower. The yellow color is like the hue of the kaṇikāra flower. The red color is like the hue of the indagopaka insect. The black color is like the hue of collyrium. The white color is like the hue of the morning star. By 'yatthā ca akkhilomāni patiṭṭhitāni' is meant the place where the eyelashes, having taken root, stand up. That is blue, deep blue: here, 'nīla' is spoken of in an all-inclusive sense.
